reader.decision: Turn on `touch_on_request` in production (set it to true in config/prod.yaml). Do not move the touch into `auth-service` now.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the cause is that `last_seen_at` never updates because `touch_on_request` is false, and `session-gc` is correct. Flipping the existing flag fixes that directly. The message gives no reason to build a new touch in `auth-service`.

reconstruction.problem: Active users are logged out about 30 minutes after login. `last_seen_at` never moves, because `edge-proxy/session.py:8` calls `auth_client.touch` only when `touch_on_request` is true, and `config/prod.yaml:1` sets it to false. `session-gc` runs every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`) and deletes sessions whose `last_seen_at` is older than `IDLE_LIMIT` of 30 minutes. My timezone theory was wrong: `session-gc` uses UTC-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and the column is `timestamptz`, so no local time is compared.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Sessions look idle, so `session-gc` deletes them and users land on the login page mid-work.
reconstruction.fix: Aelita recommends setting `touch_on_request` to true in production. The alternative is moving the touch into `auth-service`.

follow_up_questions: What does enabling `touch_on_request` cost? For example, is there extra load on `auth-service` from a touch call on every request?
Why is `touch_on_request` false in prod? Was it turned off deliberately, for example for load?
reader.closing_answer: Turn on `touch_on_request` in production. The cause is that the flag is false, so flipping it is the smallest fix. Moving the touch into `auth-service` is a larger change with no stated benefit. I would still check the load cost and why it was off before rolling out.
